description: A proposed modification of the curated Boston Dynamics Spot spec — a what-if build, not fitted hardware: an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano computer and an RPLIDAR A1 2D lidar on a 3D-printed mount post, placed on the body top and powered from the robot's pack through a 5 V buck converter. The wiring block below is ONLY this payload circuit; the robot's factory harness stays undocumented and is not drawn. The payload circuit is graded in the recorded harness report for this build; the added mass is UNKNOWN — the parts catalog records no mass for any part, so no mass total is stated for the modified robot.
name: Boston Dynamics Spot — Jetson Orin + LiDAR build

wiring.note: PROPOSED payload circuit for the Jetson + LiDAR what-if build — not the robot's factory harness, which is proprietary and undocumented (the base spec carries no wiring block, and none is invented here). Part ratings come from the parts catalog (buck_converter_5v, jetson_orin_nano, rplidar_a1). Cable gauges and lengths are design choices for the proposed build, labelled proposed in the connection labels; currents are stated only where the catalog's own numbers derive them. One finding is visible before any check runs: the catalog's 5 V buck is rated 24 V maximum on its input, and the pack rail is 50.4 V nominal / 58.8 V max — as drawn, this build needs a wider-input regulator, and the viewer flags the feed red for exactly that reason.
